Step-1:  Choose the parent hydride and assign position 1  
• The highest-priority substituent present is the carboxylic acid, so the parent is benzoic acid and the –COOH group is fixed at position 1.

Step-2:  Place the remaining substituents as required by the description  
• The aldehyde (-CHO) and the cyano (-CN) groups are each meta (1,3-) to the –COOH and also meta to one another; therefore they must be at positions 3 and 5.  
• The hydroxyl (-OH) and the dimethyl­amino (-NMe₂) groups are ortho (1,2- and 1,6-) to the carboxyl.  
• The methoxy (-OMe) group is para (1,4-) to the carboxyl.  
• In addition, both the methoxy (position 4) and the hydroxy (position 2) have to be ortho to the nitrile; hence the nitrile must be at position 3.

Thus the ring is numbered:  
1 – COOH  
2 – OH  
3 – CN  
4 – OMe  
5 – CHO  
6 – NMe₂

Step-3:  Check the numbering direction  
If the ring were numbered in the opposite direction the locant sequence for the same set of substituents would start 5-, giving the set (5,2,3,6,4) vs the set (3,6,5,2,4) obtained above.  Because 3 < 5, the chosen direction (giving 3,6,5,2,4) is the lower set and is therefore correct.

Step-4:  Arrange the substituent prefixes alphabetically (ignoring the multiplying prefix “di-” in dimethylamino is not required by many texts; treating “dimethylamino” as starting with D is conventional in such problems).  Using that convention:

cyano (C)  
(dimethyl)amino (D)  
formyl (F)  
hydroxy (H)  
methoxy (M)

Step-5:  Assemble the name  
3-cyano-6-(dimethylamino)-5-formyl-2-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzoic acid

This exactly matches option (C).

Answer: C
